clue.text: Englishspa todraw the Spanish should be drier

parts.note: Bath is the historic spa city in Somerset, England (the print runs the words together)
to tow is to draw or pull along (the print runs the words together)
el is the Spanish word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone at an English spa is told to haul the Spaniard out to dry off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be' links wordplay to definition; BATH is a Somerset city famous for its Roman baths.
explanation.definitionFit: A drier is anything used for drying, and a large cloth for after bathing fits that description.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of British

parts.note: a land is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered British prime minister calls an election by going to the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' links the leader's letter to the land; 'goes to the country' is the British phrase for calling an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmy weather is mild and soothing, as is something gentle and inoffensive.

parts.note: to cast is to throw
over can mean on account of, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: An actor dropped from the cast for some reason.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard or abandon someone, such as a lover, is to reject them.

clue.text: … sunburn — thanks to horse or equivalent

parts.note: a tan is the bronzing of skin from the sun
ta is British informal for thank you
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A trailing phrase about getting sunburnt from riding a horse, or something like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'or' are links; TA is everyday British slang for 'thanks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tantamount to another thing amounts to the same, i.e. is equivalent in effect.

clue.text: Be careful we hear in Somerset

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: watch it is a warning to be careful

explanation.surface: A warning to take care while visiting Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, the warning 'watch it' gives the name of a small harbour town on the Somerset coast in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition names the county where the town lies, a place found in Somerset.

clue.text: Beast over ten fluctuating and flickering

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece that is over another is written above it, so first

parts.note: a lamb is a young animal, a beast in the broad sense

indicators.note: fluctuating letters keep shifting about, so the three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature above a wavering number in some flickering light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluctuating' rearranges TEN into ENT, written under LAMB because 'over' places the beast first in a down answer; 'and' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lambent flame plays lightly over a surface, flickering softly.

clue.text: Drank a lot back at the base

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read this word in the other direction

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, so toped means drank a lot

explanation.surface: Soldiers drinking heavily back at the base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TOPED into the answer; 'at the' links it to 'base'.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a military base or storage station.

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is on board

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off during a party on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' links definition and wordplay; DOSS is British slang for sleeping rough or in makeshift quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: To doss down is to bed down for the night somewhere improvised.

clue.text: Enquiry into how small pair received New Year honour

indicators.note: the pair received the honour, so the honour follows it

parts.note: pr is a short form of pair
OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is awarded in the New Year Honours list

explanation.surface: An investigation into how a couple came to be awarded honours in the New Year list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into how' links; the OBE is a British award announced in twice-yearly honours lists, one at New Year.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is an investigation or searching inquiry.

clue.text: Drudgery involved in taking press to factory

parts.note: to tread is to press down with the feet
a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill

explanation.surface: The tedium of taking the printing press over to the works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in taking' and 'to' link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A wearisome repetitive routine is called a treadmill, like the wheel turned by walking.

parts.note: Apr is the short form of April

explanation.surface: A month passed acting on a stage that juts out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' links the abbreviated month to ON.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the part of the stage jutting in front of the curtain is called by this term.

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor; with the 's it gives MBS
to tone something down is to temper it

explanation.surface: A tribute to a doctor's bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravestone is a memorial marking where someone lies buried.

parts.note: to sink is to go down

indicators.note: transformed letters are changed into a new shape, so these six are reordered

explanation.surface: A scruffy drinker sees the ale changed in the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like a kitchen sink but is the verb, going down; 'transformed' is the anagram signal on 'the ale'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose shoes are worn at the back looks shabby, hence the idiom for a seedy appearance.

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Heading for London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links; London's West End is the theatre and shopping district.
explanation.definitionFit: To wend one's way is to proceed or travel in a chosen direction.

clue.text: For a certainty it's a falcon about to be released

definitions.text: it's a falcon about to be released

explanation.surface: A falconer is sure of the hawk on the glove just before letting it fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush' makes the phrase mean something certain; literally a hawk on the falconer's glove.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb sets a sure possession against uncertain gains, and a hawk held before flight is literally held on the glove.

parts.note: to shift is to move
out means determined, as in out to win

explanation.surface: A move made by someone determined to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links; 'leave' is the definition, in the sense of vacating a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate a home or office is to quit it permanently.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Silence for the workers .' gives no parse for MECHANICS: only 'workers' defines it, and nothing found in search restores the missing wordplay.

clue.text: Stumble over ell processed oil N Africa

indicators.note: the stumble is placed over, i.e. before, the rest

parts.note: to trip is to stumble

indicators.note: oil that is processed is refined into a new form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone trips on spilt oil at a refinery in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'ell' is an OCR misread of 'oil'; 'processed' signals the anagram, and 'over' sets the stumble before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Libya is a city on the North African coast.

clue.text: … one of whom is producing effects

parts.note: continuing the previous clue, this points to one of the workers, a factory hand

explanation.surface: A continuation describing one worker whose job is to make things happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue follows on from 14-down's workers: one of them is a worker, and the same word as an adjective means having effect.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative clause or drug is one that takes effect; as a noun the word means a skilled factory hand.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '\u0000across the columns enter monopoly': the opening is garbled, so the definition and the inserted O's source are missing; no reprint found.

explanation.surface: Somewhere to do one's studying in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: READING is a large town in Berkshire, west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Study of books is perusal; the second describes a Berkshire town close to the capital.

clue.text: Occupy pub they say and live

indicators.note: they say marks the pub's word as taken by its sound

parts.note: an inn is a pub
to dwell is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone told to take over the pub and live there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To indwell is to inhabit, to reside within, as a spirit fills a body.

clue.text: Lack of energy — still one gets over a…

indicators.note: in a down entry, one gets over the next piece by sitting above it

parts.note: inert means motionless or still
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tired person, motionless, gets over some trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness, the reluctance to move or act.

parts.note: AC stands for alternating current
ME is the abbreviation for the Middle East

explanation.surface: A Middle-East summit on current affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak.

indicators.note: that sounds tells the solver the next word is taken by its sound

parts.note: meet is an old word for suitable, so meeter means more suitable

explanation.surface: A trailing phrase about a measure that seems more appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meet' is archaic for fitting, so 'more suitable' gives MEETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter is an instrument that measures, such as a gas meter.

clue.text: Speak lightly of scene just shot without result

parts.note: a take is one filming of a scene
in vain means fruitlessly

explanation.surface: A film director complaining about a scene shot for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the commandment against taking the Lord's name in vain.
explanation.definitionFit: To use a name disrespectfully or flippantly is to speak of it without due reverence.

explanation.surface: Nobody wants the church job.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop after 'Nobody's' is a print flaw; 'wanting' links the two senses. Nones is the service said at the ninth hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is a possessive of 'no one'; the second is the canonical hour said at mid-afternoon in the Christian daily office.

explanation.surface: A polite request to submit an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: As in 'pray, who are you?', an old-fashioned polite form of 'please tell me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is an archaic polite request; the second means to plead with a deity or ruler.

clue.text: Ban on TNT ? I cried fit to burst

indicators.note: something fit to burst is about to explode, so these letters are blown apart and reformed

explanation.surface: A ban on explosives prompts someone to cry fit to burst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit to burst' rearranges TNT I CRIED; 'on' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdict is a formal prohibition.

parts.note: a lie is a fabrication
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A Pole is discovered telling some odd untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' links; 'Pole' is N for the north pole, not a person from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign, unfamiliar or odd.

parts.note: St, street, is a way or road
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A haphazard way to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray shot is an occasional or haphazard one.

clue.text: A lot of dollars point way to magnificence

parts.note: a grand is a thousand dollars
a ness is a headland or point

explanation.surface: Lots of money shows the way to splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way to' links; NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificence is splendour or impressive greatness.
